title: Prognostic evaluation with data in chronic kidney disease
summary:
Chronic kidney disease is one of the most common non-communicable chronic diseases and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and high healthcare costs. It affects approximately 10% of the adult global population and is therefore among the leading causes of death worldwide.

Early identification of high-risk patients is crucial to prevent or delay disease progression, the need for renal replacement therapy, and cardiovascular events. For this purpose, data from routine clinical care are used to validate a prognostic score developed on the basis of data from a large German health insurance fund.

interventions.name: This is a retrospective data analysis of clinically collected routine data.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The following data will be collected: demographic characteristics; CKD stage and etiology; comorbidities; vital parameters and body mass index (BMI); laboratory-based markers, long-term medication; and the utilization of inpatient and outpatient services at the University Hospital Bonn.
Exclusion criteria:
Kidney transplantation or pre-existing dependence on dialysis.
